adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/core/EventManager.ts:117-119 — Crash (TypeError) when evt.destinationCalendar is null/empty with Google Meet location because mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and .integration is accessed; should fall back to integrations:daily like the old code

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:253-256 — Inverted fallback in updateEvent: when externalCalendarId is falsy, the find compares cal.externalId === undefined and never matches, so calendar.events.update is called with calendarId: undefined instead of falling back to event.destinationCalendar?.externalId

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent, the new fallback logic is `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null), the `find` compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will not match normal string `externalId`s, yielding `undefined`. The previous code correctly fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`; the new code does not provide an equivalent fallback (e.g., first destination calendar or primary), so it can pass an undefined calendarId to `calendar.events.update`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:312-315 — Same inverted fallback in deleteEvent: when externalCalendarId is not provided, the find matches nothing and deleteEvent is invoked with calendarId: undefined, orphaning calendar events on cancellation/reschedule-delete

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new `deleteEvent` calendarId selection is incorrect:

```ts
const calendarId = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

When `externalCalendarId` is not provided (falsy), the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, so it will usually match nothing and yield `undefined`. Unlike `createEvent`, this path does not fall back to `"primary"` (even though `defaultCalendarId` is declared), so `calendar.events.delete` can be invoked with `calendarId: undefined`, breaking deletion for events without an explicit `externalCalendarId` reference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:148-152 — Slug logic inverted: slug is now set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true instead of when billing is disabled, causing orgs created without a slug while requestedSlug metadata condition stays the same (confidence 75: may be intentional)

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts` changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which is a clear inversion of the previous condition. As a result, when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false (the case that previously wrote `slug`), the `slug` field will no longer be set at all, while `requestedSlug` in `metadata` remains gated on `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` (same as before). This is a concrete behavior change that can lead to organizations being created without a slug in the non-team-billing path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1080 — Collective members' destination calendars silently dropped: when evt.destinationCalendar is null, ?.push is a silent no-op so teamDestinationCalendars are discarded and collective events aren't created on every member's calendar

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts the event is built with `destinationCalendar: ... : null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set. Immediately after, for collective team events it does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is null, this optional-chained push is a no-op, so the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are dropped. This prevents the new multi-destination behavior (creating events on each member’s chosen destination calendar) from being applied in that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:71, packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:127, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:155 — Non-Google services ignore the new credentialId parameter and always use the first (main host's) destination calendar, so for collective bookings with multiple O365/Lark/CalDav hosts, member credentials write to the wrong calendar or fail silently

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Calendar.createEvent` to accept a `credentialId` and updates GoogleCalendarService to select the destination calendar matching that `credentialId` (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), but non-Google implementations do not use the new parameter and instead always take the first destination calendar. In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` derives `eventsUrl` from `[mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`, i.e., only the first entry. In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent`/`createAttendees`/`updateEvent`/`deleteEvent` similarly use only the first destination calendar’s `externalId`. In `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` (CalDav/base), calendar selection is filtered using only the first destination calendar’s `externalId`. Meanwhile, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` for collective events and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, but `CalendarManager.createEvent` ignores the passed `externalId` and always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. Net effect: for multiple destination calendars, non-Google services will create/update/delete using the main host destination calendar rather than the member’s matching destination calendar, which can write to the wrong calendar or fail.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tautological find makes selectedCalendar undefined in Google update/delete: in packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts (~lines 253-256 and ~314-317), when externalCalendarId is falsy the fallback searches destinationCalendar for a cal whose externalId equals that falsy value, never matching, so selectedCalendar is undefined and the Google API is called with calendarId: undefined; updates/deletes for bookings without a stored externalCalendarId will fail

adjudication_records.issue_text: Office365 CalendarService.ts:72-76, Lark CalendarService.ts:128-129, and lib/CalendarService.ts:156-163 use destinationCalendar[0] and ignore the credentialId parameter, causing every credential in createAllCalendarEvents to write a duplicate event to the main host's calendar while teammates' calendars never receive events for collective bookings

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:1003-1010/1085-1087: organizer's and teammates' destination calendars are combined without deduplication, so a teammate sharing the same credential+externalId as the organizer causes createEvent to be invoked twice against the same calendar, producing duplicate calendar events

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, for COLLECTIVE team events the code builds evt.destinationCalendar from the organizer/eventType calendar and then appends teammates’ destinationCalendar entries via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` with no deduplication (by credentialId+externalId or similar). In EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, the new logic iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and calls `createEvent(...)` per entry, without checking for duplicates. Therefore, if the array contains two entries referring to the same calendar target (e.g., same `credentialId` and `externalId`), createEvent can be invoked twice against the same calendar, creating duplicate events.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Removed optional chaining on evt.destinationCalendar destructure in EventManager.ts:117-118 causes TypeError crash when destinationCalendar is null/empty, breaking the Meet fallback to Daily path for users without calendars (old code safely used evt.destinationCalendar?.integration)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the new code does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`/`undefined` or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and `.integration` will throw a `TypeError`. This is a regression from the old safe check `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`, and the diff shows several call sites can set `destinationCalendar` to `null` or `[]` (e.g. `handleNewBooking` sets it to `null` when none; other paths set `[]`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Google CalendarService.ts:255-257 and 314-316: find() compares cal.externalId === externalCalendarId where externalCalendarId is known to be falsy in that branch, making selectedCalendar always undefined and silently deleting the previous destinationCalendar?.externalId fallback, regressing updateEvent/deleteEvent on reschedule/cancel paths

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.updateEvent and deleteEvent, the new fallback logic is incorrect: when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, it executes `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, but `externalCalendarId` is undefined/null in that branch, so `.find()` will almost always return undefined. This removes the prior behavior of falling back to the event’s destination calendar externalId, causing updates/deletes to target an undefined calendarId (or inadvertently fall back to default behavior depending on downstream handling), which can break reschedule/cancel paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Inverted conditional spread in organizations/create.handler.ts:148-152: IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED conditions flipped polarity relative to original !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED checks, causing org slugs to be set/unset opposite to intended behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `organizations/create.handler.ts` changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which flips when `slug` is set. Previously, `slug` was set only when team billing was NOT enabled; now it is set only when team billing IS enabled. Additionally, `requestedSlug` used to be set only when team billing WAS enabled, but now `slug` and `requestedSlug` are both set when enabled and neither is set when disabled. This is an inverted/changed conditional behavior relative to the original logic and can cause slugs to be set/unset opposite to prior intended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] credentialId parameter leaked into generic Calendar interface (Calendar.d.ts:221, CalendarManager.ts:220) exists only for GoogleCalendarService's multi-credential selection; should resolve the correct destination calendar before calling the service

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the generic Calendar interface to require `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` in `packages/types/Calendar.d.ts`, and `CalendarManager.createEvent` now always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. In this diff, the new `credentialId` argument is only used by `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent` to select the correct destination calendar (`destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), while other calendar services (e.g., Lark/Office365) continue to treat destination calendar as a single/first element and don't need credential-based selection. This supports the finding as an architectural/scope concern: a Google-specific selection mechanism is pushed into the shared interface rather than resolving the destination/externalId before calling the provider service.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces repeated patterns like `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` / ternary array destructuring across multiple files (e.g., GoogleCalendarService.createEvent/updateEvent, LarkCalendarService create/update/delete, Office365CalendarService.createEvent, BaseCalendarService, EventManager, BrokenIntegrationEmail). []` vs length-checked ternary), so a helper to centralize “pick the main host destination calendar” would reduce duplication and make future changes less error-prone. adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] destinationCalendar → [x]/[] wrapping ternary logic copy-pasted in ~9 places (bookingReminder.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, webhook.ts, etc.) with subtle inconsistencies (one returns null instead of [] in handleNewBooking.ts:1067); should be normalized into shared logic

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows repeated, copy-pasted wrapping of `destinationCalendar` into an array across many call sites (e.g. `bookingReminder.ts`, `packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts`, `paypal-webhook.ts`, several TRPC handlers, `handleCancelBooking.ts`). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Credential-from-DB fetch block duplicated 3× with divergent shapes: EventManager copies include app slug in select, but handleCancelBooking.ts:~424 fetches without the app include and assigns raw Prisma result; extract a getCredentialById/getCredentialWithApp helper

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows duplicated “fetch credential from DB” logic with different query shapes and assignments. In `EventManager` (both `createAllCalendarEvents` and the calendar-reference update loop), it does `prisma.credential.findUnique({ include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}}})` and then maps the result into a custom object including `appName`. In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, it does `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` (no app include) and assigns the raw Prisma credential directly to `calendarCredential`. This matches the finding: duplication with divergent shapes, suggesting a helper would reduce drift. From the diff alone this is maintainability/consistency risk rather than a provable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In EventManager.ts updateCalendarReferences (~508-522), credential may still be undefined after DB fallback yet updateEvent is called unconditionally, unlike the guarded createAllCalendarEvents path; also credential is a loop-external let reused across iterations, allowing stale values to mask failed lookups

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.ts within updateCalendarReferences, inside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop, when `reference.credentialId` is present the code attempts to resolve `credential` from `this.calendarCredentials` and then via a Prisma fallback, but it calls `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, ...))` regardless of whether `credential` was actually found. If both lookups fail, `credential` remains `undefined`, so `updateEvent` is invoked with an undefined credential (unlike createAllCalendarEvents which guards with `if (credential)`). This is a concrete runtime correctness issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] destinationCalendar type widened to array but persistence still stores only the first element: handleNewBooking.ts:1874-1877 connects only destinationCalendar[0], so collective members' calendars are never linked to the booking record; in-memory type and persisted model have diverged

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly widens `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to `DestinationCalendar[] | null` (types + class), and `handleNewBooking.ts` now pushes additional team members’ destination calendars for COLLECTIVE events (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting the booking, it still only connects the first element (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`), so any additional destination calendars added to the array are dropped at persistence time. This is a concrete divergence between the in-memory event structure and what gets stored on the booking record.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] schedulingType added to CalendarEvent type (Calendar.d.ts:182, handleNewBooking.ts:1073) with no visible consumer in the diff; dead surface area on a core type

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `schedulingType?: SchedulingType | null` to the core `CalendarEvent` type (packages/types/Calendar.d.ts) and sets it when building `evt` in handleNewBooking.ts, but there is no diff-visible code that reads/branches on `evt.schedulingType` afterward (EventManager/CalendarManager/calendar service changes don’t reference it). This increases surface area on a central type without an evident use in this PR, which is a maintainability/scope concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] handleNewBooking.ts:688-689 replaces SchedulingType enum comparisons with raw string literals ['COLLECTIVE', 'ROUND_ROBIN'].includes(...), losing compile-time safety; also imports DestinationCalendar from @prisma/client as a type instead of the domain type in packages/types, a layering leak

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `handleNewBooking.ts` changing `isTeamEventType` from `eventType.schedulingType === SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE/ROUND_ROBIN` to `!!eventType.schedulingType && ["COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"].includes(eventType.schedulingType)`, which replaces enum-based comparisons with raw string literals, reducing compile-time/type safety. The diff also adds `import type ... DestinationCalendar from "@prisma/client"`, which is consistent with the finding’s note about potentially leaking ORM-layer types into higher-level logic (an architecture/layering concern), though whether a different domain type should be used is not fully verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Hidden side effect in handleNewBooking.ts:988-996: teamDestinationCalendars.push(...) mutates outer state from inside the attendee-mapping teamMemberPromises map, ordering-dependent and burying calendar-collection concern in an unrelated transformation

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `teamDestinationCalendars` is declared outside and then mutated inside the `users.slice(1).map(async (user) => { ... teamDestinationCalendars.push(user.destinationCalendar) ... })` that otherwise builds `teamMembers` (diff around the new `teamDestinationCalendars` and `teamMemberPromises`). This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/clarity issue: it hides a stateful calendar-collection side-effect inside an unrelated “build team member + translation” transformation. However, the claim that it is "ordering-dependent" is not clearly supported here because the `push` occurs before the first `await` in the async callback, so it will run in the synchronous map iteration order. Still, it’s a legitimate scope/architecture concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] credentialId fallback removed in CreateUpdateResult mapping (EventManager.ts ~168, 207): result.credentialId ?? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId became result.credentialId ?? undefined, so adapters omitting credentialId persist booking references without one and later updates fall into the legacy try-every-credential branch

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId` as a fallback in two CreateUpdateResult mappings, but for calendar events `result.credentialId` is now reliably populated by `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts#createEvent`, which unconditionally returns `{ credentialId: credential.id }` and is what `EventManager#createAllCalendarEvents` uses to create calendar events. Therefore the claim that “adapters omitting credentialId” will cause persisted booking references without one is not verifiable from the diff; credentialId no longer depends on adapters or `evt.destinationCalendar` in the shown flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Crash when destinationCalendar is an empty array and location is Google Meet: destructuring yields undefined and mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration throws TypeError, breaking booking creation/confirmation (packages/core/EventManager.ts:117-118)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the new logic treats `destinationCalendar` as an array: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then unconditionally accesses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` in `if (evt.location === MeetLocationType && mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar")`. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is an empty array (which this diff explicitly introduces in multiple places, e.g. `destinationCalendar: selectedDestinationCalendar ? [selectedDestinationCalendar] : []`), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, so `.integration` will throw a `TypeError`. This matches the reported crash scenario when location is Google Meet and destinationCalendar is empty.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google deleteEvent fallback is logically dead: in the fallback branch externalCalendarId is falsy, so cal.externalId === externalCalendarId can never match, making calendarId undefined and the delete call fail, leaving orphaned calendar events (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~312)

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.deleteEvent`, the fallback branch computes `calendarId` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the `.find(...)` compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will not match normal calendars, so `calendarId` becomes `undefined`. That makes the fallback effectively non-functional and can cause deletes to be issued without a valid calendarId (risking failed deletes / orphaned events). Same logical issue appears in `updateEvent`’s `selectedCalendar` fallback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google updateEvent has the same dead fallback as deleteEvent: cal.externalId === externalCalendarId can never match when externalCalendarId is falsy, yielding calendarId undefined (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~253)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent` now computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null), the fallback `find` compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined/null`), which will not match any normal `externalId`, so `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined`. This is a dead/incorrect fallback introduced by the diff (previously it fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` when it was a single object). The same pattern appears in `deleteEvent` too, and can lead to an undefined calendarId unless separately defaulted elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale credential variable reused across loop iterations in updateAllCalendarEvents: credential declared outside the loop keeps the previous iteration's value when a reference.credentialId cannot be resolved, potentially updating an event on the wrong user's calendar with wrong auth (packages/core/EventManager.ts:~495-530)

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts the update flow was changed to iterate over multiple calendar references, but `credential` is declared once outside the `for (const reference of calendarReference)` loop (`let calendarReference: PartialReference[] | undefined = undefined, credential;`). Inside the loop, when `reference.credentialId` is set, it assigns `credential = ...[0]` and, if not found, tries to fetch from DB; however, if both lookups fail, `credential` is never reset to `undefined` and the code still executes `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));`. This can reuse the previous iteration’s credential and update the wrong calendar with the wrong auth.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-Google providers only use destinationCalendar[0]: Office365, Lark, and CalDav BaseCalendarService still hardcode mainHostDestinationCalendar, so collective bookings with multiple same-provider calendars target the wrong calendar (401/404 for O365, silently skipped for CalDav) (packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:72-76, packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:127-128, packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-163)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates destinations and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`, implying per-credential/per-destination targeting. However, non-Google providers still select only the first destination calendar: Office365 uses `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and builds the URL from `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (apps-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), Lark similarly derives `calendarId` from only `[0]` (app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts), and CalDav `BaseCalendarService` filters calendars using only `[0].externalId` (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts). With multiple destination calendars for the same provider (e.g., collective bookings), later iterations will still use destinationCalendar[0], causing events to be created/updated/deleted against the wrong calendar or skipped, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED logic in org creation: when billing is disabled, organizations are created with no slug at all; when enabled, slug and metadata.requestedSlug are both set despite being previously mutually exclusive; unrelated to the PR's purpose (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151)

This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same inversion of the IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED condition affecting org creation: slug is missing when billing is disabled, and when enabled both slug and metadata.requestedSlug are set (previously mutually exclusive). This matches the golden issue of inverted logic causing both properties set in enabled case and neither in disabled case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Collective members' destination calendars silently dropped when organizer/eventType have none: evt.destinationCalendar is null so the optional-chained .push on teamDestinationCalendars is a silent no-op, discarding collected per-member data (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1084)

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Later, for COLLECTIVE team events, member calendars are accumulated into `teamDestinationCalendars`, but the code uses `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. If evt.destinationCalendar is `null`, this becomes a silent no-op and the collected member destination calendars are dropped, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google createEvent silently falls back to 'primary' when no destination matches the credential, creating the event on the wrong calendar and recording no externalCalendarId in the booking reference (packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~152-155)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now selects the target calendar via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and then uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. If no destinationCalendar entry matches the passed `credentialId` (e.g., entries lack `credentialId` or it’s undefined/mismatched), the event is inserted into the user's `primary` calendar silently. Separately, `CalendarManager.createEvent` only propagates `externalId` when the caller passes it; in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the branch where `destination.credentialId` is missing calls `createEvent(c, event)` without an `externalId`, and `EventManager` now records `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`, so booking references can end up with no externalCalendarId even though an event was created (potentially on the wrong calendar).

adjudication_records.issue_text: DB-fetched credentials silently skipped unless app.slug exists: a credential with missing app relation causes the destination to be silently skipped with no event created and nothing logged (packages/core/EventManager.ts:~345-360, also updateAllCalendarEvents and handleCancelBooking.ts)

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts (createAllCalendarEvents), when a destination has credentialId but it isn’t found in this.calendarCredentials, the code fetches it from DB with `include: { app: { select: { slug: true }}}` and only reconstructs `credential` if `credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug` is truthy. If the credential exists but has a missing/nullable `app` relation (or slug), `credential` remains undefined and the destination is silently skipped (no createEvent call, no log). The same pattern appears in updateAllCalendarEvents’ new DB fetch block. This can lead to calendar events not being created/updated with no visibility, i.e., broken behavior/data loss for those destinations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Merge-reschedule deletes only the first old calendar reference: cleanup still uses booking.references.find with singular match, orphaning all old calendar events except the first for collective bookings (packages/core/EventManager.ts:~530-535)

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts, after refactoring calendarReference to be an array (filter of all "_calendar" references) and iterating over all references for updates, the merge-cleanup path still uses a singular lookup: `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));` inside `if (newBookingId)`. With multiple calendar references (e.g., collective bookings), this will only target the first matched reference for deletion, leaving the rest of the old calendar events orphaned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cancellation recurring-branch re-executes per reference: the recurring/allRemainingBookings branch inside the per-reference loop ignores the reference and runs the entire deletion set N times, duplicating delete API calls and apiDeletes entries (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~437-455)

adjudication.rationale: In packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts, bookingCalendarReference is changed to an array via .filter(...includes("_calendar")). The code then loops `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. Inside that per-reference loop, the recurring/allRemainingBookings branch (`if (bookingToDelete.eventType?.recurringEvent && bookingToDelete.recurringEventId && allRemainingBookings)`) builds `promises` over *all* `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...endsWith("_calendar"))` and then for *all* `updatedBookings` deletes their calendar refs, pushing results into `apiDeletes`. This recurring branch does not use the current `reference`’s `uid/externalCalendarId` and will therefore re-run the full deletion set once per reference, duplicating delete API calls and `apiDeletes` entries when multiple calendar references exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organization select dropped from dynamic-link user query: loadUsers no longer fetches user.organization.slug for !eventTypeId queries, so downstream logic reading user.organization sees undefined (packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~727-742)

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, the `loadUsers` branch for `!eventTypeId` no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }` (it was explicitly present before and is removed in the new `prisma.user.findMany({ select: { ...userSelect.select, credentials: true, metadata: true } })`). This is a concrete behavioral change: `user.organization` (or at least `user.organization.slug`) will no longer be guaranteed to be available from this query unless it is already included inside `userSelect.select` (not shown in the diff). The finding’s specific downstream-undefined claim can’t be verified from the diff alone, but the dropped select itself is real and could break code that relies on it.
